text_reviewed.title: Ultrasound-guided FNAC of a thyroid nodule

steps.d: A three-dimensional view of the neck region.
The thyroid gland sits in the front of the neck, over the upper trachea.
The gland rests against the trachea, with a lobe on each side.
A nodule is an area within the gland that is being sampled.
The ultrasound probe is placed on the skin over the gland.
A fine needle is passed through the skin into the nodule. You may feel a slight pin prick from the needle.
The needle is moved back and forth within the nodule several times.
The needle is removed and an adhesive dressing is applied. The dressing stays on for 1–2 hours.
Results are usually available in 1–2 weeks.
